correctness.rationale: The normalized hollow symmetric Monge vertices are two disjoint a-by-b symmetric corner rectangles of entries 1/(2ab), as established by the primary vertex theorem. Their exact matrix inner product is 1/[2max(a,c)max(b,d)], yielding the given squared Frobenius distance. Comparable pairs telescope into positive one-coordinate expansion increments, and the discrete cubic a(n-a-1)(n-a) has a factored first difference giving the three residue-specific maxima and ties. Incomparable pairs have squared distance >=27/(4n^3), strictly greater than optimal comparable separation for every n>=4; n=3 is separately enumerated. Hence the exact all-n three-case formula, two/two/four face-crossing shortest edges, and half-distance nearest-vertex noise radius follow. A separately written exact-rational enumeration checked all 100947 pairs for n=3..21 and literal normalized matrices for n=3..6; it is not used as an infinite proof.

Their full text does not give the Frobenius minimum over vertex pairs or the residue-class equality list. A different same-day published full result computes each vertex projection onto the convex metric face and the Hausdorff gap; although it uses exactly the same Gram coefficients, it neither yields nor implies the shortest pair metric.
